text:
rachel: quick heads-up, we promoted adaptive-kernel-fusion (late-binding) to interactive clusters this morning.

rachel: TL;DR: p99 down ~17% for short/interactive routes, median down ~3%, and token compute cost down ~20% across the sampled mix.

dev: nice. can you paste the canary numbers?

rachel: canary (2h): baseline p99 = 295ms -> fusion p99 = 245ms. p50 = 43ms -> 41ms. total token-GPU units/sample -20%. kernel launch count per request -1.3.

sophie: which models/routes were in scope? exclusions?

rachel: scope: seq <= 128, prefix_kv-enabled interactive routes. Models: rwd-chat-small, rwd-chat-medium-quant, hosted-gg-6b. Excluded streaming-only, very long-context routes, and any routes opted into `route.exec_policy = "no-fusion"`.

kevin: short explain for the infra folks?

rachel: short: we do late-binding fusion of consecutive small kernels on the fast path when remainder-token budget is low and KV footprint is stable. this avoids repeated kernel setup and reduces memcpy churn. also added a safety check to skip fusion if predicted tail risk > 0.5.

rachel: config we flipped:
```
exec.fusion.mode = "late-binding"
exec.fusion.max_combined_tokens = 16
exec.fusion.tail_risk_cutoff = 0.5
```

ops-bot: canary: adaptive-kernel-fusion promoted to default in region-us-west-2 at 2027-05-04T09:22:47Z :white_check_mark:

sophie: any regressions or surprises during canary?

rachel: saw one tenant with pinned legacy kernels hit a +12% p95 blip for ~8m because their route opted out earlier; we temporarily routed them to a dedicated lane and fixed the pinning rule. also small +2% memory on older nodes, autoscaler rebalanced. no data loss.

dev: alerts/dashboards/runbook?

rachel: dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/fusion/late-binding-overview 
runbook: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/adaptive-kernel-fusion 
new alerts: exec.fusion.failed.count, exec.fusion.tail-regression.p95, exec.kernel.launchs.saved.rate. Added a 30m post-rollout watch that fires to #eng-runtime if p99 regresses >5%.

kevin: customers need to change anything?

rachel: no API change. Performance policy update: default execution policy for seq<=128 is now `fusion-late-binding`. Teams requiring per-kernel determinism can opt out with `route.exec_policy = "no-fusion"`.

sophie: can we add a dashboard widget showing how many routes opted out?

rachel: good call. creating follow-up ticket #7342 to add opt-out telemetry and #7343 to improve fusion heuristics.

kevin: please prepare a 1-paragraph blurb for #announcements with opt-out note and links.

rachel: will draft it and post tomorrow AM. big thanks to runtime + infra + sres for quick testing. :tada:

ops-bot: follow-ups logged: #7342 (fusion opt-out telemetry), #7343 (fusion heuristics tuning), #7344 (post-rollout perf checklist).

rachel: closing thread  ping me if you see unexpected p99 movement.
